entities.name: FusionAIAgenticArchitecture
observations: FusionAI implements autonomous agentic capabilities through SmolAgents framework, supporting both tool-calling and code-execution agents with multi-step reasoning.
Agents can dynamically discover and use tools from three sources: built-in Tool Registry (web search, Wikipedia, RAG), MCP servers (dynamic external tools), and code execution environment.
Processing pipeline implements Chain of Responsibility with 7 stages: input validation, load memory, MCP tools discovery, agent execution, MCP cleanup, store memory, output validation with LLM Guard.
Supports both provider-based agents (OpenAI API) and transformer-based agents (local CPU/GPU models) for flexibility and cost optimization.
Real-time updates to Portal implemented via adr-signalr-and-sticky-sessions.md with supporting ADRs on WebSocket alternatives, load balancing, scaling, and security.

entities.name: MCPDynamicToolIntegration
observations: Model Context Protocol (MCP) enables zero-code agent extension by connecting to external MCP servers via SSE transport to discover tools at runtime.
MCPToolsProcessor in pipeline connects to MCP server using mcp_server_params from request, retrieves tool schemas, and merges them with Tool Registry tools.
MCPCleanupProcessor ensures proper disconnect after pipeline execution to avoid resource leaks and stale connections.
Supports authenticated MCP servers via mcp_auth_token with Bearer token header injection, enabling secure enterprise integration.
Tools discovered from MCP are treated identically to built-in tools, maintaining uniform agent execution regardless of tool source.

All MCP servers support stdio or SSE transport for integration with VS Code GitHub Copilot and other MCP clients

entities.name: AgentProcessingPipeline
observations: Seven-stage pipeline: InputValidationProcessor, LoadAgentMemoryProcessor, MCPToolsProcessor, AgentExecutionProcessor, MCPCleanupProcessor, StoreAgentMemoryProcessor, OutputValidationProcessor.
Each processor implements execute(request, context) returning bool to continue/stop pipeline, enabling fail-fast on validation errors.
Context dictionary passes data between stages: agent, mcp_tools, mcp_client, result, token_usage, error.
Memory processors integrate with Redis via HistoryManagerFactory supporting pluggable backends (Redis, in-memory cache).
Agent execution processor combines Tool Registry tools with MCP tools, runs agent with custom_instructions (system_prompt), and tracks token usage via monitor.

entities.name: M365CopilotIntegrationStrategy
observations: Architectural guidance for integrating Microsoft 365 Copilot context with external agents like GitHub Copilot in VS Code
Key insight: Cannot export M365 Copilot's internal context (Semantic Index/grounding) directly - must provide access to same underlying data sources (SharePoint/Microsoft Graph)

Four integration paths identified: 1) Extend M365 Copilot with agents/connectors (Microsoft-native), 2) Build GitHub Copilot Extension/MCP tool querying Graph (practical for dev teams), 3) Index/sync SharePoint to repos (operationally easy but risky), 4) BYOK for LLM choice (not for data access)
Path 2 (MCP tool for Graph) most aligned with Yorizon FusionAI agentic architecture - leverages existing MCPDynamicToolIntegration patterns
M365 Copilot extensibility uses: agents, Copilot connectors (ingest external data into Graph), plugins/actions - requires Copilot Studio
Warning: Connectors/agents may trigger cost and IT/InfoSec review depending on data consumed
2026-01-19: Path 2 (MCP tool for Graph) implemented as MCP365Service
Key learning: Enterprise tenants often require admin consent for ALL unverified apps, making Graph Explorer token the practical workaround
Azure CLI cannot request arbitrary Graph scopes - fixed scope set excludes Mail.Read, Files.Read, Calendars.Read by Microsoft design (GraphExplorerFirstPartyPrivilege concept)

entities.name: MCPGraphToolPattern
observations: Pattern for GitHub Copilot Extension/MCP tool that queries Microsoft Graph/SharePoint on-demand
Architecture: VS Code/GitHub Copilot Chat -> MCP server/Copilot Extension -> Microsoft Graph/SharePoint (permission-trimmed) -> short excerpts + links -> Copilot uses as context
Implementation requirements: Entra ID authentication, permission trimming (user sees only what they're allowed), content shaping (short, relevant, attributable excerpts)
This approach shares DATA not M365 Copilot's internal semantic index - effectively a 'Graph-powered retrieval tool'
MCP explicitly intended for 'integrating with other systems' per GitHub documentation
Aligns with FusionAI MCPDynamicToolIntegration practice - tools discovered at runtime via SSE transport

entities.name: MCP365Authentication
observations: Multi-strategy authentication supporting 4 methods prioritized by availability
Option 1: Graph Explorer Token (RECOMMENDED) - Full M365 permissions, 1-hour expiry, requires manual refresh
Option 2: Azure CLI - Automatic refresh but LIMITED scopes (User, Groups, Sites listing only - NO Mail/Calendar/Files)
Option 3: Custom App with Admin Consent - Full access, permanent, requires IT approval
Option 4: Client Credentials - App-only access for service accounts, requires admin consent
Enterprise tenant constraint: Many tenants require admin consent for ALL unverified (non-Microsoft-published) apps
Graph Explorer special: Pre-authorized by Microsoft as first-party app, enables user consent without admin approval
Azure CLI limitation: Fixed scope set for Azure infrastructure management, intentionally excludes personal data APIs (Mail.Read, Files.Read, Calendars.Read)

entities.name: MCP365CapabilityDetection
observations: GraphClient.checkCapabilities() probes available permissions at runtime
Tracks failed endpoints (403/401) in failedEndpoints Set to avoid repeated failures
PermissionError class provides helpful context: required permissions, affected endpoint, resolution guidance
m365_status tool exposes capability detection to users via MCP
safeRequest() method returns null instead of throwing for optional data that can gracefully degrade
ENDPOINT_PERMISSIONS mapping defines required scopes per API pattern (/me/messages -> Mail.Read, etc.)

Commands: npm run token:status (check validity/expiry), npm run token:refresh (prompt for new token)
JWT decoding to extract: user (upn), expiry (exp), scopes (scp), app (app_displayname)
Auto-saves token to .env file after validation
5-minute buffer before expiry to warn users proactively
Displays scope availability for important permissions: Mail.Read, Files.Read, Sites.Read, Calendars.Read, User.Read
